ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ passes through the vertices A and C of the square OABC. Given that the coordinates of point A are $\left(1, -3\right)$, what is the value of $b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $CM \perp x$-axis at point M, and construct $AN \perp y$-axis at point N. \\
Hence, $\angle OMC = \angle ONA$, \\
Since quadrilateral OABC is a square, \\
Thus, $OA=OC$, $\angle AOC=90^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle COM + \angle MOA = \angle MOA + \angle NOA = 90^\circ$, \\
Therefore, $\angle NOA = \angle COM$, \\
Also, since $OA=OC$, \\
Therefore, $Rt\triangle OCM \cong Rt\triangle OAN$ (AAS), \\
Thus, $OM=ON$, $CM=AN$, \\
Since the coordinate of point A is $(1, -3)$, \\
Therefore, $AN=1$, $ON=3$, \\
Thus, $OM=3$, $CM=1$, \\
Hence, the coordinate of point C is $(3, 1)$, \\
Substituting the coordinates of points A and C into $y=kx+b$, \\
We obtain $\begin{cases}k+b=-3 \\ 3k+b=1\end{cases}$, \\
Solving gives: $\begin{cases}k=2 \\ b=\boxed{-5}\end{cases}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: O is at the coordinate origin, square OABC has OA and OC as adjacent sides, with A below the x-axis and C above the x-axis to the right; the graph of y=kx+b crosses both A and C. From the text, A=(1,-3). Let C=(u,v). Since OA and OC are adjacent sides of a square, they are perpendicular and have equal length. Therefore (1,-3)·(u,v)=0, so u-3v=0, and u^2+v^2=1^2+(-3)^2=10. The image shows C in the first quadrant, so take the positive solution v=1, u=3, hence C=(3,1). Then the line through A and C has equations -3=k+b and 1=3k+b, yielding k=2 and b=-5.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中坐标系原点 O 在两轴交点处，正方形 OABC 以 O 为一个顶点，点 A 位于 x 轴下方且在右侧，点 C 位于 x 轴上方且在右侧；直线 y = kx + b 经过 A 和 C。

再推理：已知 A = (1, -3)，所以向量 OA = (1, -3)。因为 OABC 是正方形，OA 与 OC 是邻边，因此 OA ⟂ OC 且 |OA| = |OC|。设 C = (u, v)，则有
(1, -3) · (u, v) = 0，得到 u - 3v = 0；
又因为 |OC|^2 = |OA|^2 = 1^2 + (-3)^2 = 10，所以 u^2 + v^2 = 10。
联立 u = 3v，可得 9v^2 + v^2 = 10，故 v^2 = 1。结合图像中 C 在第一象限，取 v = 1，于是 u = 3，所以 C = (3, 1)。

将 A(1, -3) 与 C(3, 1) 代入直线 y = kx + b：
-3 = k + b，
1 = 3k + b。
两式相减得 4 = 2k，因此 k = 2，再代回得 b = -5。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ passes through the vertices A and C of the square OABC. Given that the coordinates of point A are $\left(1, -3\right)$, what is the value of $b$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $CM \perp x$-axis at point M, and construct $AN \perp y$-axis at point N. \\
Hence, $\angle OMC = \angle ONA$, \\
Since quadrilateral OABC is a square, \\
Thus, $OA=OC$, $\angle AOC=90^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle COM + \angle MOA = \angle MOA + \angle NOA = 90^\circ$, \\
Therefore, $\angle NOA = \angle COM$, \\
Also, since $OA=OC$, \\
Therefore, $Rt\triangle OCM \cong Rt\triangle OAN$ (AAS), \\
Thus, $OM=ON$, $CM=AN$, \\
Since the coordinate of point A is $(1, -3)$, \\
Therefore, $AN=1$, $ON=3$, \\
Thus, $OM=3$, $CM=1$, \\
Hence, the coordinate of point C is $(3, 1)$, \\
Substituting the coordinates of points A and C into $y=kx+b$, \\
We obtain $\begin{cases}k+b=-3 \\ 3k+b=1\end{cases}$, \\
Solving gives: $\begin{cases}k=2 \\ b=\boxed{-5}\end{cases}$
